reuse.why: The link-guard is one shared helper called by every provider, but Fintegra linking and download are verbatim copies of the Pluggy.ai functions and the takeover unlink restates unlinkAccount's field reset instead of reusing it.

duplication.why: linkFintegraAccount (~70 lines) copies linkPluggyAiAccount, downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadPluggyAiTransactions, and the unlink field-set and 'not found' check repeat unlinkAccount and the link functions.

placement.why: Guards, link handler and download live in accounts/app.ts and sync.ts beside their siblings, though a function named assert* also performs the unlink mutation.

scope.why: Focused on the four steps; the client-side additions (readable name, fintegra:false) are needed only to satisfy the provider record types.

maintainability.why: One guard for all providers is good, but it now mixes closed-account validation, duplicate detection and unlinking behind a misleading name and a boolean flag, and the provider code grows by copy-paste.

bypasses_abstraction.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked resets the previous holder's link fields with its own db.updateAccount instead of going through the existing unlinkAccount handler.

disguised_duplication.where: The copied Fintegra link/download functions and the unlink field reset are plain copies, not renamed or reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains the replaceExistingLink boolean (step 4) plus a closed-target branch (step 3) and a takeover/unlink branch (step 4); all six link handlers call it.
